task.title: Separate the GLM delegate's response budget, provider output ceiling and repository read budget
task.objective: The glm-delegate MCP server conflates three different limits behind one name and hard-codes a 64000-token response ceiling, so GLM 5.3's large input context is unusable: at most 240,000 bytes of repository source can be assembled per delegation and no caller can ever request more than 64000 output tokens. Split the concepts into a default response budget (16384), a configurable provider output ceiling (131072) and a substantially larger repository read budget (200,000 bytes per file, 1,500,000 bytes total, 120 files), all environment-configurable and sanity-validated, then prove the change with executed local tests and a real GLM delegation. The architecture target is LARGE INPUT, COMPACT OUTPUT: a big repository slice in, a normally 8K-24K report out. No security, containment, secret-filtering, governance or read-only guarantee may be weakened.

architecture: Three limits must stay separate concepts with separate names and separate environment variables: GLM_MCP_MAX_TOKENS is the default response budget, GLM_MCP_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS is the provider/model output ceiling, and GLM_MCP_MAX_FILE_BYTES / GLM_MCP_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES / GLM_MCP_MAX_FILES are the repository input budget. Never label two of them 'Max tokens'.
The hard-coded 64000 response ceiling is removed and no arbitrary 64K clamp may be reintroduced anywhere. The effective budget is max(512, min(requested, provider ceiling)).
Configuration is resolved once per delegation and passed into _expand_scope() and read_scope_text(); environment values must not be re-parsed inside inner file-processing loops.
Python standard library only. No new dependency of any kind.
The larger output ceiling exists for exceptional investigation only. The default response budget stays conservative at 16384 so ordinary delegations stay compact for the Manager's context.
security: SECRET_NAME_HINTS must not be weakened, and secret-bearing path rejection must keep matching every segment of the repository-relative path, not just the basename.
Repository-root containment must not be broadened. Paths outside the root stay refused.

The Z.AI credential is read from GLM_API_KEY only and is never hardcoded, printed, logged, returned or committed. glm_status keeps reporting presence only. The real credential must not be invalidated by any test.
The delegate stays read-only: no shell execution, no filesystem writes, no Git writes, no test execution, no Beads ownership, no write-lease ownership, no orchestration, no recursive delegation.

Raising the read budget increases how much repository source leaves the machine per delegation. Skipped build/output directories, readable-suffix filtering, truncation notices, omission notices and scope-too-wide notices must all survive.
compatibility: No product behavior, IPC contract, preload API, persisted shape or public contract changes. This is developer-agent tooling outside the packaged runtime.
MCP protocol compatibility is preserved: initialize, tools/list and tools/call still work and glm_delegate, glm_review and glm_status all stay exposed.
offline: AWKIT's offline-first production guarantee is unchanged. The delegation server and its verifiers are developer tooling only; nothing under app/, src/ or the packaged runtime may reference them. The live verifier requires the public internet and is registered as such, following the verify:wdu-live precedent.

acceptance.description: The default response budget, the provider output ceiling and the repository read budget are three independently configurable settings; the 64000 hard cap is gone; max_tokens=100000 resolves to an effective budget of 100000 against the default 131072 ceiling; max_tokens=200000 clamps to 131072; a configured ceiling of 32768 clamps a requested 64000 down to 32768; malformed and out-of-range environment values fall back safely.

A single delegation can assemble and send more than the old 240,000-byte total, bounded by the configured per-file, total-byte and file-count limits, with truncation and omission notices intact and secret-bearing and out-of-root paths still refused.

A real glm_delegate call over that large scope, run through the MCP stdio path against a freshly started server, returns a coherent bounded report within a requested 16384-token budget, with provider-reported input and output token counts and stop reason recorded verbatim.

glm_status reports every setting under a distinct name, glm_review still returns its CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/OBSERVATION structure with the larger read capacity, at least one failure path clamps or fails predictably with a useful diagnostic instead of crashing, and no repository write capability was introduced.

evidence.artifact: The bare `python -m py_compile .claude/mcp/glm_delegate_server.py` invocation is refused by the write-lease guard, which blocks bare `python`/`node` script execution. The identical assertion is executed inside verify:glm-delegate as check PC-1, 'glm_delegate_server.py byte-compiles (py_compile, doraise)', which passed. The recorded command is the one that actually ran, not the one originally planned.
91 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 BLOCKED. Offline: the two HTTP-boundary checks stub urllib, so no credential and no network are used.

40 PASS / 5 FAIL / 0 BLOCKED (45 checks), exit 1. Delegation failures: LD-7 and LD2-7 (stop_reason=max_tokens, not end_turn) and LD-8 (report structure found 4 of 6: Summary, Files inspected, Implementation details, Assumptions). Measured root cause, shared with the review failures: GLM 5.3 bills unrendered `thinking` blocks against the output budget (59100 and 49143 characters of thinking on the two delegations), so the shipped default 16384 budget is consumed before the report is finished. The large-input half of the change is proven — LD-2 sent 432572 bytes and LD2-2 sent 287972 bytes, both far past the old 240000-byte ceiling, with the server's own accounting matching the local survey exactly. NOT relabelled as PASS.

Same run. Review failures: RV-L3 (the CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/OBSERVATION structure is missing MEDIUM, LOW and OBSERVATION) and RV-L5b (stop_reason=max_tokens). 73667 characters of unrendered thinking against a 16384 budget left only 2561 characters of visible report. This is the GLM-CTX-NO-REGRESSION acceptance criterion and it is NOT met.

verify:glm-delegate and verify:glm-delegate-live registered in scripts/lib/verifier-classification.ts as class "integration", written by the project-state actor under this lease (the manager actor may not write a lease-scoped path). Rationale is evidence-backed, not asserted: verify_glm_delegate.py really spawns the server with subprocess.Popen and drives the MCP initialize/tools-list/tools-call handshake over stdio against tempfile.mkdtemp fixture trees it actually writes, stubbing urllib only at the HTTP boundary - so it is neither static-source-validation (never executed) nor unit (in-process fakes, no subprocess). Precedents cited and confirmed present in the same file: verify:oracle-live (integration, credential-gated against a REAL database) and verify:wdu-live (external-dependency wording; real-browser only because it launches a browser, which these do not). Verifier green: all 5 checks passed, 202 of 202 verify:/validate: scripts classified, no stale entries. Per-class counts 1 documentation-consistency / 11 static-source-validation / 63 unit / 39 integration / 77 real-browser / 11 packaged-application / 0 clean-machine-acceptance.

completion.notes: PHASE 2 ACTIVE. Phase 1 (manager, .claude/mcp tooling + the package.json npm-script relaxation through SHARED_WRITE_PATHS) is written and released; its offline evidence passed. The writer is now project-state for scripts/lib/verifier-classification.ts and the docs/roadmap reconciliation, which the manager actor may not write. THIS TASK IS NOT COMPLETE AND MUST NOT BE CLOSED: glm-live-delegation and glm-live-review are recorded FAIL, so acceptance GLM-CTX-COMPACT-OUTPUT and GLM-CTX-NO-REGRESSION are unproven. The measured cause is a real product gap, not a test defect — GLM 5.3 bills unrendered `thinking` against the output budget, so the shipped 16384 default cannot both reason and finish a structured report. Remedy for a later tranche, deliberately NOT attempted here because it is outside the awkit-rkd8 mandate that reopened this lease: either raise the shipped default, or exclude reasoning from the budget the contract advertises. Phase 2's own scope is limited to registering the two new verifiers so verify:verifier-classification stops failing repo-wide, which is a required closeout gate for every task and currently blocks awkit-rkd8.
